Semantic summary: a bigger battle-presentation sub-effect than 080d59b0. Opens one display window (id 46), copies a palette/tile block through a generic word-copy helper (Func_080072f0 taking the 0x03001388 word-copy routine as a callback argument, matching the WordCopy idiom already established in 080e7404.c), then blanks a 1024-slot shared confetti pool at 0x02010000 (laid out as up to 8 members x 128 slots, 28 bytes each, matching the stride already established in 080d59b0). For each active party member it seeds that member's 128-slot sub-range with randomized polar-coordinate confetti (Func_08002322/Func_0800231c sine/cosine calls) around a position derived from Func_080e3944. The main loop then runs member_count*20+56 times: near the start of each member's staggered window it cues a portrait-swap sound and Func_080d6888, then for every later pass it advances and redraws that member's confetti slots through Func_080072f4/Func_080e3908, expiring slots whose lifetime field crosses a threshold.

New this pass: heap_cache (the *(void**)0x03001EEC-derived pointer, kept in r5 across the whole prologue in the reference) is reused for FOUR distinct derived reads, not just the two/three previously modeled -- cursor-advance for work/draw_destination, heap_cache[2] for extra_target, heap_cache-108 for facing, and heap_cache+28 for draw_rectangle_fn. This is a stronger, more general version of the 'shared work-block header' idea already flagged for promotion in 080d82b0's own prior pass and 080e01e4's dossier; worth folding into a shared header/idiom note for the whole 0x03001eec family rather than re-deriving per owner.

New this pass: materializing an intermediate 'target_slot = (void**)((u8*)work+0x7828)' pointer variable, even when duplicated verbatim at each use site to avoid apparent aliasing, gets silently CSE'd/hoisted by this compiler across the whole extended block (including across the branch into the loop body), producing an extra stack spill/reload of the address that the reference does not have. Writing every access as a fresh M2C_FIELD(work, void**, 0x7828) expression instead (never assigning the intermediate address to its own named variable) avoided the CSE and let the compiler's native register-offset addressing selection reproduce more of the reference's instruction shapes. This is a stronger, more general lesson than 080e01e4's 'DrawRectangleFn[2] split' note and likely explains part of why 080d59b0 and 080dc1ec still carry unresolved dh -- worth checking both for an equivalent persistent-slot-pointer local that could be inlined away the same way.

Two open, evidence-backed questions carried over from 080d59b0/080dc1ec/080e01e4 and not resolved here either: why this compiler passes what looks like a 5th call argument through r4 (reconfirmed again at this owner's own Func_080072f4 site, with the w/h arguments on the stack beyond it), and why the reference keeps the shared work pointer in r9 while this compiler's candidate keeps choosing a different register for it in places. A third, related but distinct residual observed for the first time here: even after matching the source shape, the register allocator's choice of WHICH high register (r8/r9/sl/fp) holds which loop-invariant local address across a large loop body does not always match the reference's choice, and the scheduler's order for a run of independent immediate-load instructions feeding a single call (e.g. Func_080ed408's four register arguments) does not always match the reference's order either, even though the values, registers, and net effect are all otherwise identical. Both read as compiler-internal list-scheduling/register-allocation heuristics rather than anything expressible as a source-shape difference; not chased further this pass per the project's guidance against open-ended permutation search.

One nearly-tautological reference conditional was preserved literally rather than simplified: `if (member_count * 20 != -56) ...` gates the whole main loop and is true for every realistic non-negative member_count, but the reference genuinely computes it that way (count<<2 + count, then <<2 again, compared to -56), so it is kept as literal arithmetic rather than rewritten to `if (member_count != 0)` or similar, since the point is to reproduce the compiled shape, not simplify the source.
